The global nuclear sector reached a structural turning point in 2025, moving from policy exploration into a high-speed deployment phase. Driven by the massive energy demands of AI infrastructure, the World Bank’s historic shift to fund nuclear projects, and the rise of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), the industry is scaling to meet a projected doubling of capacity by 2050. To understand the strategic opportunities in emerging markets and next-gen fuel technologies, explore the full report.

✅ Hyperscalers are securing 24/7 baseload power through major nuclear PPAs, with AI clusters now requiring up to 100 MW each.

✅ The World Bank and Asian Development Bank have officially normalized nuclear financing, unlocking institutional capital for global projects.

✅ Indonesia, Philippines, and Vietnam are moving into active execution, targeting 8.5 GW by 2037.

✅ Egypt’s El-Dabaa project and South Africa’s 5.2 GW mandate represent a $105 billion commercial opportunity.

✅ Belgium, Italy, and Greece are restarting or initiating nuclear programs to ensure energy sovereignty.

✅ The shift toward HALEU and Accident Tolerant Fuels is de-risking advanced reactor deployment and shortening timelines.

Read the complete analysis 👉 https://t.co/7MEp2OINFm
